name: Tessoval Lemongrass-Tamarind Fizz
description: A budget sour fizz from Primark's mid-tier portfolio, combining synth-lemongrass and synth-tamarind for a bright, acidic profile aimed at Tier 1-2 consumers who want complexity without premium cost.
flavor_profile: Sharp citrus-herb lemongrass opening, then a deep tangy tamarind pull with a slightly metallic synth finish
cultural_context: Tessoval is a workhorse brand — widely available, rarely celebrated. the Gray Zone kids mix it with powdered supplements to stretch nutritional value. The slightly metallic synth finish is a known quality control issue Primark has never bothered to fix.
story_hooks: A batch of Tessoval from a specific production run has an unusual compound in it — not dangerous, but it causes mild synesthesia in users with unshielded BCIs, and word is spreading fast in the Gray Zone.
A Tier 4 food anthropologist is writing a paper about Tessoval as 'accidental folk culture' — her presence in the Gray Zone doing research is causing tensions.
Primark's internal documents show they've known about the metallic finish issue for eleven years and calculated it's cheaper to keep the defect than to fix the production line.
